exposure: maternal blood inflammatory markers (C-reactive protein, systemic immune-inflammation index, systemic inflammation response index)
outcome: rates of delivery at < 28, < 32, < 34, and < 37 weeks of gestation
cohort: The study included 141 patients diagnosed with cervical incompetence who underwent either ultrasound- or physical examination-indicated transvaginal cervical cerclage between January 2020 and December 2022.
finding: Ultrasound-indicated cervical cerclage was associated with better pregnancy and neonatal outcomes compared to physical examination-indicated cerclage, and twin pregnancy and increased maternal inflammatory markers (CRP, SII) were identified as risk factors for preterm delivery before 34 weeks.
